inputs.userGoal: Build only Tenant 2 Azure Storage with SFTP enabled
subGoals: Security-first: SSH public-key authentication, no SFTP password, no anonymous blob access, and no public network access.
Brownfield-safe: preserve the supplied Tenant 1 VM, network, and deployment sources unchanged.
Cross-tenant-ready: output the Storage resource ID and SFTP endpoint for a later Tenant 1 private endpoint request.
insightsApplied: insight-001: Kept the Tenant 1 resource group out of scope and made the Tenant 2 Storage resource ID an output for the later private endpoint request.
insight-002: Retained the Tenant 1 VNet; the future consumer-side deployment will place and resolve the private endpoint there.
insight-007: Retained the Windows VM and exposed connection details for its future WinSCP configuration.

resources.name: st-sftp-tenant2
resources.subtype: StorageV2 with SFTP and hierarchical namespace

reasoning.whyChosen: SFTP requires a general-purpose v2 or premium block blob account with hierarchical namespace enabled. StorageV2 Standard_LRS is the simplest supported baseline, while public access, anonymous access, and account-key authorization are disabled.
alternativesConsidered: Premium BlockBlobStorage for higher transaction performance
reasoning.tradeoffs: LRS minimizes cost but does not provide zone-level durability. SFTP can constrain geo-redundant failover scenarios, so GRS/GZRS is not selected by default.

references.title: Enable SFTP support in Azure Blob Storage
Architecture best practices for Azure Blob Storage

resources.name: default-blob-service

reasoning.whyChosen: The blob service is the parent for the private SFTP home container.
alternativesConsidered: Use the implicit blob service without declaring it
reasoning.tradeoffs: Declaring the child service makes the container dependency explicit and provides a future location for service-level data-protection settings.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The blob service is a child of the Storage account.

resources.name: sftp-data
resources.subtype: Private blob container and SFTP home directory

reasoning.whyChosen: A dedicated private container bounds the local user's SFTP permission scope and provides a deterministic home directory.
alternativesConsidered: Create separate upload and download containers
reasoning.tradeoffs: One container is simpler but does not separate inbound and outbound data lifecycles.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The container is a child of the default blob service.

resources.name: sftp-user

reasoning.whyChosen: The SFTP protocol uses Storage local users. SSH public-key authentication avoids generated passwords, and permissions are limited to the dedicated container.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Local users do not integrate with Microsoft Entra RBAC. The selected permissions allow normal file transfer and deletion; ownership and ACL modification remain denied.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The user is a child of the Storage account and its permission scope and home directory reference the container.

overallReasoning.summary: Create only the producer-side Tenant 2 SFTP service. The deployment provisions a hardened Azure Storage account, private container, and least-privilege SSH-key local user. It deliberately does not create Tenant 1 networking. A later Tenant 1 deployment will use the emitted Storage resource ID to request a blob private endpoint, which Tenant 2 must approve.
overallReasoning.tradeoffs: Monitoring and diagnostic settings are omitted because no Log Analytics destination was supplied and the requested scope is Storage SFTP only. Customer-managed keys and Key Vault are omitted; Microsoft-managed encryption remains enabled and no secret is generated because authentication is SSH-key-only. Standard_LRS is the cost baseline; select Standard_ZRS if zone durability is required. Soft delete, versioning, and point-in-time restore are not enabled by default because SFTP workflows commonly rename and delete files and retention requirements were not supplied. Insights 003-006 describe retained Tenant 1 subnet, public IP, NSG, and NIC resources; they are intentionally not applied because the user selected a Tenant 2-only build.

plan.validation: All dependencies resolve in deployment order: Storage account -> blob service -> private container -> local user. StorageV2, hierarchical namespace, and SFTP properties are compatible. Public network access is disabled, so no data-plane connection succeeds until a private endpoint is created and approved. The generated Bicep must compile with zero errors and pass Checkov with no unresolved high or critical findings before it is offered for deployment.
architecturePrinciples: No secrets in source or deployment output
